diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-1 Body construction
diagrams.description: Exploded view of the main outer body panels and subassemblies showing front apron, hood, front fenders, doors, side windows, cowl top grille, body main unit, and tail gate.
measurements_and_specs: Wheelbase difference: GS30 is 300 mm (11.81 in) longer than S30
diagrams.mechanic_notes: GS30 2+2 model has an extended wheelbase and floor pan extension between front and rear floors; door and tail gate panels differ from S30 2-seater.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-2 Structure of body main unit
diagrams.description: Perspective isometric cutaway of the welded unibody shell assembly (body main unit) showing structural members, cowl, floor pan, tunnel, rear wheelhouses, and roof pillars.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Shows the unitized body shell construction. Provides primary reference structure for underbody tramming and collision repair.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-3 Underbody alignment for S30 (2 seater)
diagrams.description: Comprehensive dimensional blueprint of underbody datum lines, diagonal checks, width measurements, and vertical reference heights for the S30 (2-seater) chassis, detailing measuring points 'A', 'B', 'C', and 'D'.
components: Hood ledge front strut installing unit
Engine installing unit (front side / rear side)
Gear case mounting front crossmember locate hole unit

callouts.A point: Front strut mounting and engine cradle forward datum location
callouts.B point: Front side member reference datum location
callouts.C point: Floor pan / gear case crossmember reference datum location
callouts.D point: Rear strut tower installing unit reference datum location

measurements_and_specs: Front track / frame width: 700 mm (27.56 in)
Front crossmember locating hole distance: 600 mm (23.62 in)
Diagonal front engine bay: 1,148.6 mm (45.22 in)
Front-to-rear floor span: 1,385 mm (54.53 in)
Rear crossmember width: 780 mm (30.71 in), 836.4 mm (32.93 in)
Unit: mm (in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: All measurements are symmetrical along car center line. Tram gauge must be maintained parallel to underbody plane. Unit is mm (in).

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-4 Underbody alignment for GS30 (2 + 2 seater)
diagrams.description: Comprehensive dimensional blueprint of underbody datum lines, diagonal checks, width measurements, and vertical reference heights for the GS30 (2+2 seater) chassis, showing extended 300 mm floor dimensions.
components: Hood ledge front strut installing unit
Engine installing unit (front side / rear side)
Gear case mounting front crossmember locate hole unit

callouts.A point: Front strut mounting and engine cradle forward datum location
callouts.B point: Front side member reference datum location
callouts.C point: Floor pan / gear case crossmember reference datum location
callouts.D point: Rear strut tower installing unit reference datum location

measurements_and_specs: Wheelbase extended by 300 mm (11.81 in) over S30
Front-to-rear floor span: 1,685 mm (66.34 in) vs 1,385 mm (54.53 in)
Diagonal measurements: 2,419.8 mm (95.27 in), 2,053.0 mm (80.83 in)
Overall span reference: 2,217 mm (87.28 in)
Unit: mm (in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Points A, B, C, D follow identical reference geometry as S30 except for the 300 mm (11.81 in) extension in the floor pan between dash lower panel and rear floor.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-5 Exploded view of front bumper
diagrams.description: Exploded view showing front bumper bar, side bumper ends, shock absorber struts, shims, rubber and metal sight shields, and overrider brackets.
measurements_and_specs: Impact capability: 8 km/h (5 MPH) solid barrier
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Gas-and-oil-filled shock absorbers must not be drilled, disassembled, or heated.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-6 Exploded view of rear bumper
diagrams.description: Exploded view showing rear bumper assembly, shock absorbers, tie-down hooks, shims, side bumpers, and sight shields.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Includes rear tie-down hooks LH and RH mounted with the bumper shock absorbers.

diagrams.caption: Bumper system inspection chart
diagrams.description: Flowchart for inspecting bumper appearance, measuring bumper height, checking shock absorber dimensions (compressed and expanded), checking operation, and replacing shock absorbers if faulty.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Guide to systematically evaluate bumper alignment, stroke, and shock absorber condition.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-7 Standard height of front bumper
diagrams.description: Measurement diagram showing front bumper height from ground line under curb weight conditions.
measurements_and_specs: Front bumper standard height: 438 to 477 mm (17.24 to 18.78 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Measure under curb weight conditions with tires inflated to rated pressure.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-8 Standard height of rear bumper
diagrams.description: Measurement diagram showing rear bumper height from ground line under curb weight conditions.
measurements_and_specs: Rear bumper standard height: 438 to 477 mm (17.24 to 18.78 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Measure under curb weight conditions with tires inflated to rated pressure.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-9 Length of shock absorber
diagrams.description: Dimensional drawing of front and rear bumper shock absorber exposed shaft/bracket length.
measurements_and_specs: Front shock absorber standard length: 86 to 90 mm (3.39 to 3.54 in)
Rear shock absorber standard length: 86 to 90 mm (3.39 to 3.54 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Unit: mm (in). If dimension is out of range, shock absorber has failed to return or is collapsed.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-10 Checking shock absorber function
diagrams.description: Illustration showing screw jack positioned against solid wall and bumper overrider to compress bumper shock absorber 40 mm.
measurements_and_specs: Stroke: approx. 40 mm (1.57 in)
Jack capacity: > 400 kg (881 lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Caution: Do not allow jack to slip out of overrider. Ensure parking brake is set and wheels chocked.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-11 Removing front side bumper securing nut
diagrams.description: Location of nuts securing front side bumper through inner fender protector.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Loosen three screws on inner fender protector to reach the two side bumper nuts.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-12 Removing front bumper
diagrams.description: Removing two nuts per side securing front bumper assembly to shock absorber mounts.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove two nuts securing bumper to shock absorber brackets.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-13 Removing shock absorber
diagrams.description: Loosening three bolts securing front bumper shock absorber to front side frame member.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove horn before unbolting shock absorber.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-14 Removing rear bumper
diagrams.description: Removing rear bumper assembly from rear shock absorber brackets.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove side bumper plugs and bolts before removing bumper to shock absorber nuts.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-15 Removing shock absorber
diagrams.description: Removing rear shock absorber bolts and withdrawing unit through opening in car body.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Requires removal of fuel tank and muffler (Section FE).

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-16 Clearances between muffler and L.H. shock absorber heat shield (California models)
diagrams.description: Clearance diagram for California exhaust system around muffler, shock absorber bracket, spare tire housing, and heat shield plates.
measurements_and_specs: Muffler to shock absorber bracket: 24 mm (0.94 in), Min.: 8 mm (0.31 in)
Muffler to spare tire housing: 21 mm (0.83 in), Min.: 10 mm (0.39 in)
Unit: mm (in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: California models only: check heat shield clearances carefully to prevent exhaust overheating of rear body components.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-17 Removing center grille upper bar attaching screw
diagrams.description: Accessing center grille upper bar screw after moving front combination lamp cover inside.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Loosen two combination lamp cover screws to reach upper grille bar screw.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-18 Removing center grille
diagrams.description: Locations of four screws securing center radiator grille.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove four screws securing center grille in place.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-19 Removing lower grille
diagrams.description: Locations of three screws securing lower radiator grille.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove three screws securing lower grille.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-20 Adjusting hood attaching bolts
diagrams.description: Loosening hood hinge attaching bolts to adjust fore-and-aft position of the hood.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Adjust fore and aft position before setting lock and bumper heights.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-21 Adjusting hood bumper height
diagrams.description: Adjusting rubber bumper height on cowl ledge to set rear hood height flush with fenders.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Lower bumpers during initial alignment so they do not hold hood open prematurely.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-22 Adjusting hood lock male part
diagrams.description: Slotted hole adjustment of hood lock male part fore/aft and side-to-side.
measurements_and_specs: Attaching bolts torque: 0.38 to 0.51 kg-m (2.7 to 3.7 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Loosen bolts just enough to slide male part into perfect alignment with female receiver.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-23 Safety catch lever
diagrams.description: Safety catch lever engagement clearances with hood lock female part.
measurements_and_specs: Clearance A: 5.0 mm (0.197 in)
Clearance B: 8.0 mm (0.315 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Verify safety catch lever reliably retains hood when main lock is disengaged.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-24 Sectional view of hood lock
diagrams.description: Cross section through hood lock male and female components showing dovetail bolt, springs, cushion rubber, and release lever.
measurements_and_specs: Lock nut of dovetail bolt torque: 1.5 to 2.6 kg-m (11 to 19 ft-lb)
Male & female part attaching bolts torque: 0.38 to 0.51 kg-m (2.7 to 3.7 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Dovetail bolt height sets the rear hood pull-down clearance (1 to 3 mm below fender top).

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-25 Lubricating points
diagrams.description: Lubricating points on hood safety catch lever, female lever pivot, and return spring.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Lubricate shaded points with multi-purpose grease to ensure smooth engagement and prevent unlatching.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-26 Removing hood
diagrams.description: Supporting hood and removing bolts securing hood hinge to hood.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Mark hinge location before removing bolts to aid reinstallation.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-27 Removing hood torsion bar
diagrams.description: Disengaging end of hood hinge counterbalance torsion bar using a screwdriver.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Support hood securely before releasing torsion bar tension.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-28 Hood lock
diagrams.description: Exploded view of the complete hood lock mechanism, release wire, knob, bracket, and male/female latches.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Shows the routing of the hood release cable through cowl grommet to the interior knob.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-29 Removing cowl top grille
diagrams.description: Lifting the front edge of the cowl top grille and pulling forward to disengage from windshield lower edge.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Wiper arms must be removed prior to pulling cowl grille forward.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-30 Removing front fender
diagrams.description: Exploded view showing front fender assembly, headlight case, front fender front extension, inspection lid, inner protector, and attaching fastener locations.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Fasteners: side sill (2), front pillar (1), cowl top (2), hood bumper (2), hood ledge (3).

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-31 Structural view of tail gate
diagrams.description: Exploded structural view of tail gate assembly, hinges, shims, gas stay, latch lock, key cylinder, down stopper, and striker.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Hinges are split type. Tail gate stay is gas-pressurized; handle with care.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-32 Adjusting tail gate hinge
diagrams.description: Adjusting tail gate hinge position and adding or removing shims to set roof-to-tailgate gap.
measurements_and_specs: Roof-to-tail gate clearance: 3.5 to 5.5 mm (0.138 to 0.217 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Insert shims between hinge and body for fore-and-aft adjustment.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-33 Adjusting striker
diagrams.description: Loosening tail gate striker screws and moving striker vertically to flush tailgate with fenders.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove license lamp first to gain access to striker adjusting screws.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-34 Adjusting tail gate lock
diagrams.description: Adjusting tail gate latch lock mechanism alignment to prevent binding on striker.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Test operation by opening and closing tail gate two or three times before final tightening.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-35 Adjusting down stopper
diagrams.description: Forward and rearward slotted adjustment of the tailgate down stopper.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Down stopper adjusts in forward/rearward directions only.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-36 Removing nuts attaching rear combination lamp to body
diagrams.description: Accessing rear combination lamp mounting nuts from inside luggage compartment.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Disconnect wiring connector before removing attaching nuts.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-37 Removing license lamp
diagrams.description: Removing screws securing license lamp to rear panel.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Detach lamp assembly after loosening screws.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-38 Removing rivets
diagrams.description: Method of pushing out center pin of plastic rivets on rear panel finisher using a small punch and hammer.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Push center pin in to release expansion collar of the rivet.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-39 Removing finisher and combination lamp assembly
diagrams.description: Detaching rear finisher and combination lamp unit together from rear panel.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove as a complete assembly before separating lamps and trim rim.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-40 Adjusting door hinge
diagrams.description: Door hinge adjustment directions and allowable adjustment limits.
measurements_and_specs: Adjustment limit: Upper, lower, forward and rearward: 3 mm (0.12 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Holes in body pillar are enlarged for adjustment; hinge-to-door bolts are non-adjustable.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-41 Adjusting door lock striker
diagrams.description: Adjusting door lock striker vertically and horizontally on B-pillar.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Adjust striker only after door hinge alignment has been finalized.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-42 Adjusting door hinge
diagrams.description: Using Door Hinge Wrench ST08720000 to reach and turn door hinge body bolts without removing front fender.

callouts.ST08720000: Special Service Tool Door Hinge Wrench

measurements_and_specs: Special tool: Door Hinge Wrench ST08720000 (J 25610)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Enables door alignment and removal while front fender remains mounted on car.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-43 Removing door trim
diagrams.description: Exploded view of door trim hardware including arm rest, escutcheons, regulator handle, and retaining spring clip.
components: Rear inside handle escutcheon (GS30 2 + 2 seater only)

callouts.6: Rear inside handle escutcheon (GS30 2 + 2 seater only)

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Orient window regulator handle forward when door window is fully closed.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-44 Removing escutcheon cover
diagrams.description: Prying off inside handle escutcheon screw cover with a screwdriver.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pry carefully to prevent scarring decorative plastic escutcheon.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-45 Removing door trim
diagrams.description: Using a flat tool or screwdriver to pop door finisher retaining clips from door inner panel.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pry close to clip positions to avoid breaking fiberboard panel backing.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-46 Door window glass and regulator for S30 (2 seater)
diagrams.description: Exploded view of door window glass, sash, front and rear guide rails, guide channels A and B, regulator mechanism, and crank handle for S30 2-seater.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Specific to S30 two-seater door. Note layout of guide channel A and B mounting screws.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-47 Door window glass and regulator for GS30 (2 + 2 seater)
diagrams.description: Exploded view of door window glass, sash, front and rear guide rails, guide channels A and B, regulator mechanism, and crank handle for GS30 2+2 seater.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Specific to GS30 2+2 seater door. Different door sash and glass length from 2-seater.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-48 Guide rail adjusting mechanism
diagrams.description: Adjusting bolts and slotted holes on inner door frame for front and rear window guide rails.
measurements_and_specs: Lower bolt: tighten fully then back off 4 turns and lock
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Initial setting for lower adjusting bolt: tighten all the way, then return 4 turns and lock.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-49 Proper clearance between outside door panel and glass
diagrams.description: Cross section through door window opening showing clearance between glass outer surface and outer door panel skin.
measurements_and_specs: Clearance: 22 to 24 mm (0.87 to 0.94 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Adjust guide rail upper adjusting bolts to establish 22 to 24 mm clearance.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-50 Adjusting front and rear guide rails
diagrams.description: Fore and aft adjustment arrows for front and rear guide rails to eliminate sideways glass free play.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Move rails fore and aft to eliminate unwanted sideways glass play.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-51 Adjusting guide channel A
diagrams.description: Diagram showing glass tilt conditions (A - front tilted down, B - rear tilted down) and how adjusting guide channel A corrects parallel alignment with top rail.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Move guide channel A up for condition (A); move down for condition (B).

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-52 Removing door trim
diagrams.description: Door inner frame after removal of door trim and water screen showing access cutouts.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove water seal screen carefully to access regulator and guide channel fasteners.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-53 Removing screws attaching glass back plate to guide channel B
diagrams.description: Accessing screws connecting the door glass bottom bracket to regulator guide channel B.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Support glass securely from dropping when screws are removed.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-54 Removing guide rail
diagrams.description: Removing front and rear vertical guide rails through inner door panel access openings.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove guide rails after lifting glass upwards and out.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-55 Removing regulator assembly
diagrams.description: Withdrawing the regulator mechanism assembly through the lower inner door panel opening.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Collapse arms to maneuver mechanism through the lower stamped cutout.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-56 Door lock mechanism for S30 (2 seater)
diagrams.description: Exploded view of the door lock mechanism, rods, interior handle, and lock knob for S30 2-seater.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Single inner handle configuration for two-seater models.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-57 Door lock mechanism for GS30 (2 + 2 seater)
diagrams.description: Exploded view of door lock linkage for GS30 2+2 seater showing front remote handle, rear inside handle, rods, and lock mechanism.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: GS30 2+2 model includes an auxiliary rear inside door release handle and linkage.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-58 Adjusting outside door handle free play
diagrams.description: Adjusting nylon nut on outside handle pushrod to establish 0 to 1.0 mm clearance with lock lever.
measurements_and_specs: Clearance: 0 to 1.0 mm (0 to 0.039 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Turn nylon adjusting nut to set zero-to-minimal clearance without pre-loading latch.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-59 Adjusting inside door handle
diagrams.description: Adjusting inside door handle in elongated mounting slots with lock knob engaged.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Move handle rearward in slotted holes until it stops, then tighten screws.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-60 Removing outside door handle
diagrams.description: Loosening outside door handle attaching nuts from inner door cavity.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove handle together with vertical connecting rod.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-61 Removing door lock assembly
diagrams.description: Removing latch mechanism screws from door shut-face and withdrawing latch from inside door.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Withdraw lock assembly through access hole in inner door panel.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-62 Removing door lock striker
diagrams.description: Loosening screws securing striker plate to body pillar.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Use impact screwdriver if striker screws are excessively tight.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-63 Body side and door weatherstrips
diagrams.description: Door opening perimeter view and cross-sectional profiles of body side and door sash weatherstrips for 2-seater and 2+2 seater.

callouts.Section: A-A: Body side weatherstrip cross section on pillar flange
callouts.Section: B-B (2 seater): Door sash upper weatherstrip profile for 2-seater
callouts.Section: B-B, C-C (2 + 2 seater): Door sash upper weatherstrip profile for 2+2 seater

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Profiles differ between 2-seater and 2+2 models at section B-B/C-C.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-64 Removing body side weatherstrip
diagrams.description: Removing scuff plate and pulling body side weatherstrip off the door aperture pinchweld.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Loosen scuff plate screws before pulling weatherstrip.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-65 Prying off rivets
diagrams.description: Prying off plastic rivets retaining door weatherstrip to door sash groove using a screwdriver.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pry carefully to release rivets without tearing weatherstrip rubber channel.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-66 Front windshield glass
diagrams.description: Exploded view of front windshield glass, perimeter weatherstrip, stainless moldings, and cross section A-A showing adhesive application points.
measurements_and_specs: Apply adhesive to body flange lip and weatherstrip mating groove as shown in section A-A
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Apply adhesive to specific sealing contact points on weatherstrip before mounting glass.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-67 Removing front windshield glass
diagrams.description: Separating windshield glass adhesive bead using a spatula worked around flange from outside.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Always start removal from upper side portion to prevent sudden drop.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-68 Tools for installation of windshield glass
diagrams.description: Required hand tools for installing windshield glass: capillary tube, spatula, and draw string.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Capillary tube used for injecting adhesive into rubber channel; strong nylon string used to pull rubber lip over pinchweld.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-69 Structural view of side window for S30 (2 seater)
diagrams.description: Exploded view of fixed quarter side window, frame sash, weatherstrips, joint covers, and rubber seals for S30 2-seater.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Fixed quarter glass installation on S30 2-seater.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-70 Structural view of side window for GS30 (2 + 2 seater)
diagrams.description: Exploded view of hinged/opening rear side window glass, center pillar, upper bracket, sash, latch handle, rubber washer, and finisher nut for GS30 2+2 seater.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Hinged vent window design specific to GS30 2+2 models, utilizing pivot brackets and toggle latch handle.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-71 Structural view of tail gate glass
diagrams.description: Exploded view of tail gate glass, surrounding rubber weatherstrip, and stainless trim moldings with cross section A-A.
measurements_and_specs: Use sealing agent rather than adhesive during installation
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Use non-hardening sealing agent instead of adhesive for tailgate glass.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-72 Structural view of front and rear seats
diagrams.description: Exploded structural view of front reclining bucket seats, slide rails, and GS30 2+2 folding rear seat assembly.
measurements_and_specs: Reclining tilt: 6° forward, 36° backward, pitch 3°
Slide travel: 180 mm (7.09 in), pitch 20 mm (0.79 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Rear seatback folds flush with floor on 2+2 model.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-73 Removing front attaching bolts of front seat
diagrams.description: Removing front mounting bracket bolts securing front seat track to floor pan.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Slide seat rearward to expose front floor bracket bolts.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-74 Removing rear seat cushion
diagrams.description: Removing front securing screws to detach rear seat cushion on GS30 2+2.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: GS30 2+2 only: unscrew front retaining screws before lifting cushion.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-75 Removing rear seatback
diagrams.description: Removing hinge pivot bolts attaching rear seatback to body side structure on GS30 2+2.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Fold seatback forward and pull mat away to reach hinge mounting bolts.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-76 Removing inner lap belt
diagrams.description: Removing floor anchor bolt securing inner buckle stalk and wire harness.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Disconnect buckle switch harness connector before unbolting anchor.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-77 Removing strut cover clip
diagrams.description: Removing synthetic resin plastic clip from rear strut tower trim cover.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: S30 models: pry center pin to remove clip without breaking cover.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-78 Removing shoulder belt (for S30 2 seater models)
diagrams.description: Removing shoulder belt guide anchor bolt and escutcheon on rear strut tower for S30 2-seater.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Keep washers and spacers in proper order for reassembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-79 Removing shoulder belt (for GS30 2 + 2 seater models)
diagrams.description: Removing shoulder belt upper anchor bolt and escutcheon on B/C-pillar for GS30 2+2 seater.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Requires removal of quarter panel trim and weatherstrip to reach anchor bolt.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-80 Removing shoulder and outer lap belts
diagrams.description: Removing ELR retractor cover and two floor anchor bolts securing outer retractor unit.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Shoulder and outer lap belts are an integral retractor unit; replace as a set.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-81 Removing rear seat belts
diagrams.description: Loosening rear floor anchor bolts securing rear seat belts on GS30 2+2.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Rear seats must be removed before unbolting rear seat belt retractors.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-82 Body side trim (2 + 2 seater)
diagrams.description: Exploded view of interior body side trim panels for GS30 2+2 seater including quarter panel garnish, rail garnish, reservoir protector, and rear trim.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Use punch/skinny bar to push center pin of expansion fasteners to remove.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-83 Spare tire compartment lid
diagrams.description: Exploded view of rear floor spare tire well lid, hinges, and prop rod/support mechanism.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Flush floor mounted spare tire cover.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-84 Tail gate trim
diagrams.description: Layout of retaining clips and screws for the tailgate inner trim finisher panel.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Carefully release perimeter clips to prevent tearing trim panel.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-85 Floor console
diagrams.description: Exploded view of center floor console, shift boot opening, armrest pocket, mounting screws, and harness connections.
measurements_and_specs: 5 mounting screws
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove 5 screws and unplug wiring before lifting console over shifter.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-86 Inside rearview mirror
diagrams.description: Exploded view of inside rearview mirror, mounting bracket, base cover, and attaching screws.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pry off base cover to access mounting screws.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-87 Instrument panel
diagrams.description: Exploded view of the dashboard assembly, instrument upper garnish, padded main dashboard shell, lower brackets, and mounting hardware.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Always disconnect battery cable before beginning dash removal. Speedometer cable must be uncoupled.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-88 Removing instrument finisher
diagrams.description: Detaching center gauge / heater control instrument finisher from dash structure.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove screws securing finisher before withdrawing center panel.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-89 Instrument panel under cover
diagrams.description: Lower steering column / pedal area under-dash trim cover and retaining screws.
measurements_and_specs: 2 attaching screws
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove two screws to take down under cover.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BF-90 Sealing body panel joint
diagrams.description: Overview map and cross sections detailing factory sealer locations on body panel seams and joints (Sections A-A through H-H).

callouts.Section: A-A: Inner sill and outer sill joint
callouts.Section: B-B: Body side member, rear floor panel, and rear fender panel joint
callouts.Section: C-C: Roof panel and drip rail joint
callouts.\"D\" portion: Gasoline filler unit (Right side) - lower portion and overall circumference
callouts.Section: E-E: Rear fender panel, mud guard, tail rail main, and complement band joint
callouts.Section: F-F: Dash floor panel, dash side panel, front fender baffle, front fender panel, and door joint

troubleshooting.symptom: Bumper shock absorber fails to return to original position after compression test
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Internal binding, mechanical damage, or loss of high-pressure gas charge

troubleshooting.symptom: Door window regulator handle operating force exceeds 3.5 kg (7.7 lb)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Insufficient lubrication, incorrect glass-to-panel clearance, or misaligned/non-parallel guide rails
troubleshooting.corrective_action: (1) Lubricate guide rollers, guide rails and regulator linkage; (2) Perform weatherstrip-to-door glass adjustment; (3) Adjust guide rails in parallel

troubleshooting.symptom: Door window glass tilts forward or rearward in door sash
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Adjust guide channel A up if front tilts down (condition A), or down if rear tilts down (condition B)

troubleshooting.symptom: Seat belt buckle switch fails inspection (test light does not go out when latched or go on when unlatched)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Worn, deformed, or faulty switch contacts or internal push rod mechanism
